_README: Every human judgement about this ROM lives in this file; the
generated listings are disposable, so renaming is free.
What to do next, roughly in order:
Read the coverage it reports. Low coverage is normal at
first and is the number you are trying to move.
2. Every unresolved indirect jump it reports is a hole. Add the
target to `entries`, or the pointer pair to `ram_vectors` if
the handler is installed into RAM.
Finds the sound code and the tables feeding it.
4. Name things in `labels` as soon as you know what they are.
See docs/method.md for the working order and docs/pitfalls.md for
the traps that each cost real time.

comments.b6:8EDC: accept only if the start offset is above the current index (priority = position)
comments.b6:8F0F: the end of a sound also drops a refused request
comments.b6:A915: SongRequest is the song number itself, so song 0 cannot be requested this way
comments.b6:A87D: AUDCTL per song (every entry is 0: 64 kHz clock, no joins, no filters)
comments.b6:A7E2: sustain: no register write at all
comments.f7:F163: pause: AUDF1-4, AUDC1-4 and AUDCTL zeroed; a note held across the pause comes back with AUDF 0
comments.f7:DDEA: the main loop parks here while Paused; the DLI chain keeps running
comments.b6:B6DA: wait for the next DLI (Dli_Resync) to fire inside this one
comments.b6:A109: bonus items by map row: count b6:A163 and end index b6:A1A2 per level; rows b6:A16C, x b6:A187, sprite b6:A1AA, palette/width b6:A1C5, value b6:A1E0

headers.b6:8ED2:
SfxTick: the whole TIA effects driver (67 bytes). X = channel 1 then 0. A request (SfxReq, an id 1-11)
is taken only if its start offset in SfxStream is ABOVE the channel's current index: position in the
blob is the priority, an idle channel has index 0. A refused request stays in SfxReq until the sound
ends, which clears it. Stream: $00 end; $01-$0F set AUDC, no time; $10-$FF = AUDF (whole byte) with
AUDV = its high nibble, one frame. Called from Dli_Bottom (vblank) unless paused. (live)
headers.b6:A90E:
MusicTick: once a frame from TopDliBody (inside the top DLI), skipped while Paused. A non-zero
SongRequest starts that song and returns. Otherwise each voice in VoiceMask runs VoiceTick:
envelope step, then the note's duration, then the next note / pattern / track end. SongNow = $FF
writes AUDC = 0 on all four voices every frame. (live: model equal to the chip log for 11 songs)
headers.b6:A86F:
MusicStart: A = song. AUDCTL from SongAudctl (all 0 here), the song's 8-byte record (4 track
pointers) to TrackPtr, VoiceMask from the non-zero pointers, AUDC = 0 on all four, first pattern
and first note of each used voice.
headers.b6:A851:
TrackEnd: a track entry with a zero high byte ends it; its low byte is the command: 0 restart
this song, $80-$FF stop (SongNow = $FF), n = start song n-1. The first voice to end decides.
headers.b6:A75D:
EnvStep: five stages through a jump table (JMP (EnvJmpLo)): attack (add to an 8-bit level up to the
peak), decay (subtract down to the sustain level), sustain (counts, writes nothing), release
(subtract to 0), off (AUDC = 0 every frame). AUDC = instrument byte 0 | level >> 4. A stage's
length is a counter tested DEC / BPL, so a length of $80-$FF ends at once.
headers.b6:A8F5:
MusicReset: SKCTL = 0 then 3 (the only POKEY set-up besides the reset code's clear of
$4000-$4010), then MusicStart with ResetSongByLevel,X (X = level 0-7, 8 = title).
headers.b6:B699:
TopDliBody: CTRL, the next DLI vector, eight palette colours, MusicTick (unless Paused), then a
spin on DliSeen until Dli_Resync (the next DLI, taken INSIDE this handler) sets it: the music
tick's variable time is absorbed before the first raster-timed writes.
headers.f7:F0F8:
Dli_Bottom: the last DLI (vblank work): flip DPPL to the finished list, the Pause switch (toggle
Paused on release), bank 6 for the status code and SfxTick; while Paused it zeroes AUDV0/1 and
POKEY $4000-$4008 every frame instead. Restores the level's bank from LevelBank.
headers.f7:F009:
Dli_Top: the first DLI. Switches bank 6 in for TopDliBody (music) and the level's bank back in
(LevelBank by Level): an NMI that switches banks, not transferable to a BankSet cart.
headers.f7:F06A:
Dli_ZonePalette: one per 16-line playfield zone (11 a frame). A byte per map row (level bank
$9B80,Y for levels 0-3, $BB00,Y for 4-7): bits 5-6 pick the palette, bits 0-4 an entry of the
RAM colour tables $2751/$2764/$2777. (code)
headers.f7:F19C:
BuildRowLists: for the 17 rows on screen (Y = ScrollRow + $10 down) copy the row's staged
sprite headers into the hidden display list and add the background: ONE 5-byte indirect
object, 20 two-byte characters, whose pointer is the map row itself in the level bank (20
bytes a row). (code; the lists decoded live from a RAM dump)
headers.f7:F2A9:
DrawListAdd: A = object slot. Takes a node from the ring of 20 free node numbers (NodeTake),
links it at the tail of a doubly linked list ($256F object, $2584 next, $2598 previous, head
DrawHead, tail DrawTail), and marks the slot listed ($25AC). (code)
headers.f7:FBDD:
Fade out and display off: starts the palette fade (counter $FD, stepped in vblank by b6:B886),
waits for it, then CTRL = $7F. The main thread changes bank only after this, so the NMIs can
restore the bank from LevelBank,Level instead of a shadow. (code)

blocks.name: SfxStart
blocks.note: start offset in SfxStream per effect id (0-11); also its priority (live)

blocks.name: SfxStream
blocks.note: TIA effect streams, 196 bytes; index 0 is the idle terminator

blocks.name: DurTable
blocks.note: note lengths in frames, longest first

blocks.name: Instruments
blocks.note: 16 x 16 bytes, 10 used: AUDC base, attack frames, peak, attack add, decay frames, sustain level, decay sub, sustain frames, release frames, release sub

blocks.name: SongTracks
blocks.note: track lists (pattern pointers, ended by a zero high byte whose low byte is the command) then 43 count-prefixed patterns of 2-byte notes

blocks.name: SongTable
blocks.note: 11 songs x 4 track pointers (0 = voice unused)

blocks.name: TitleCodeImage
blocks.note: copied to RAM $1D00-$1FBF by CopyTitleCodeToRam and run there (the title screen's loop and its NMI handler at $1DEA, which switch between banks 6 and 0); not disassembled in place because it is assembled for $1D00

notes.f7:
Commando (NTSC) (Atari) (1989) (CD1A98C5).a78
mapper supergame, 128 KB, NTSC
POKEY at $4000 -- so the music is not on the TIA

Vectors: IRQ $DD67  NMI $F000  RESET $DD67

Written by init.py. Everything here is read from the cartridge; the
judgement calls are yours to add.

Study notes: fixed bank. Reset f7:DD67, main loop f7:DDDD, NMI f7:F000 -> JMP ($AE): Dli_Top f7:F009
(bank 6: music), Dli_Resync b6:B70A, Dli_ZonePalette f7:F06A x11, Dli_Bottom f7:F0F8 (flip, pause,
effects). Both sound ticks run inside NMIs that page bank 6 in and the level's bank back.
notes.b6:
Bank 6: sound (SfxTick b6:8ED2, music driver b6:A71C-A940, song data b6:A941-B698), the
top DLI's body, title and copyright screens (their code is copied to RAM), init.
Entered through the JMP table at b6:A000-A029.
notes.b0:
Bank 0: the title picture, a 160B bitmap (12 zones of 16 lines, 80 bytes a line, a page per
line, $8000-$B0EF). Paged in only by the title code that runs in RAM. (live)
notes.b1:
Bank 1: levels 1 and 5 (LevelBank f7:F8F7 = 1 2 3 4 1 2 3 4 5). Map rows of 20 two-byte
characters drawn in place, row tables at $9B00/$9B80 and $BA80/$BB00, sprites, set-piece code
($9C00), and the common block $B200-$B6A2 that banks 1-5 all carry (JMP table at $B200).
notes.b2: Bank 2: levels 2 and 6. Same layout as bank 1; traced statically only.
notes.b3: Bank 3: levels 3 and 7. Same layout as bank 1; traced statically only.
notes.b4: Bank 4: levels 4 and 8. Same layout as bank 1; traced statically only.
notes.b5:
Bank 5: entry 8 of LevelBank; its $B000 is called at each game and life start with DMA off.
Carries the common block too. Role otherwise not established.
